title: Where Does the Union Bound Go? Best-Arm Identification and Strong FWER Control
abstract: arXiv:2608.19903v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: In fixed-confidence best-arm identification, proofs often use a union bound across the competing arms. From a multiple-testing point of view this can look puzzling: if the best arm is unique, only one hypothesis of the form ``arm $i$ is best'' can be true. Why then should there be a Bonferroni-type factor of $K-1$? The answer is that there are two natural ways to orient the hypotheses. In one orientation, best-arm identification is literally a strong familywise-error-rate (FWER) problem with $K-1$ true nulls. In the opposite orientation, exactly one null is true, but a pairwise implementation can falsely reject that one null through any of $K-1$ comparisons. Thus the multiplicity has not disappeared; it just pops up in different places. This note makes the equivalence explicit in the terminology of both communities.

translated_title: 联合界去哪里了？最佳臂识别与强族错误率控制
translated_abstract: 在固定置信度最佳臂识别中，证明通常使用跨竞争臂的联合界。从多重检验的角度看，这可能令人困惑：如果最佳臂是唯一的，那么形式为“臂$i$是最佳”的假设中只有一个可以为真。为什么还需要$K-1$的Bonferroni型因子呢？答案在于有两种自然的假设定向方式。在一种定向下，最佳臂识别本质上是一个具有$K-1$个真零假设的强族错误率（FWER）问题。在相反的定向下，恰好有一个零假设为真，但成对实现可能通过$K-1$个比较中的任何一个错误地拒绝该唯一真零假设。因此，多重性并未消失，只是出现在不同的地方。本说明在两个领域的术语中明确阐述了这种等价性。
tldr: 本文澄清了最佳臂识别中联合界与多重检验的联系，指出其等价于强族错误率控制问题，并解释了多重性在不同假设定向下的表现方式。
en_tdlr: This note clarifies the connection between union bounds in best-arm identification and multiple testing, showing equivalence to strong familywise-error-rate control and explaining how multiplicity manifests differently under alternative hypothesis orientations.
